note: Diarization is badly fragmented (many '?:' lines, Amal/Medi labels swapped in places); I judged speaker from content. D5 is a mis-pairing by the compare step: r1's row inside D5 (26:38 akun -> 3am baseer) is the same row as D16, so D16 carries the grammar row and D5 is ruled only on r2's 26:19 'aswad' vocab question. The 26:19 Latin transcript cannot show a final hamza (aswad 'black' vs aswa2 'worse'), so D5 is kept low. D18 turns on a doubled t (basato vs basatto) that the Latin transliteration cannot encode and Amal echoed without a fix, so it is dropped as unverifiable rather than as 'not an error'. Several r2/r1 rows in the 30:00-52:00 conjugation drill are letter-order slips (بيسبت for بيبسط, embasana for embasatna) that the READER-BRIEF explicitly classes as S4; I dropped those (D8, D10, D12, D17, D20). D14 (بتحمس -> متحمس, B15) is a separate moment from the 03:43 بهمس -> بتحمس fix and should not be merged with it. 22:49-25:00 is a beekeeper interruption in English, not lesson content.

row.medi_said: يعني ،شو يعني شو لا-- what... What language?
row.amal_said: No بلاقي، إنتا بتلاقي، شو لقيت؟
row.why: She asked شو لقيت؟ twice (01:24, 01:31) and he decoded it as 'what language?' - he took لقيت for لغة, the word they had just been on at 00:57-01:03; she said 'No' and explained بلاقي / بتلاقي / لقيت (sheet: i found | Ana la2ait | أنا لقيت), so this is a wrong-word listening error, not a didn't-know: he never asked, he answered wrong and she corrected.

rulings.why: Both readers saw the same listening slip; tier 1 fits because he mapped her word onto a different lexical item (لغة) rather than asking for it, and her 'No' is an explicit-no, not an 'asked' signal. t=01:34 is the line that carries the wrong reading.

row.why: He meant 'the method' (research on how to learn) and said طريق; her sheet lists them as two separate words, 'road / way / route | 6ariq | طريق' and 'way / method | Tariqa | طريقة', she asked طريق أو طريقة؟ and he fixed to طريقة at 02:03.
row.english: I found a very good way / method.

rulings.why: Tier 1, not 2: طريق and طريقة are two different sheet entries with different meanings (road vs method), so he picked the wrong lexical item, not the wrong gender form of one noun.

row.medi_said: To learn would be أتأل-- or يتعلّم or-
row.why: Building 'the best way (for me) to learn' he offered the he-form يتعلّم; she said لا أتعلم (I-form), he repeated it and only THEN asked 'is that for me or just to learn?' (02:35), so the form was attempted and rejected before any question - the 'or يتعلّم' line is unlabeled ('?:') but sits inside his 'أتأل-- ... or-' turn and cannot be Amal since she answers it with لا.
row.english: (the best way) to learn / for me to learn

rulings.why: Not a didn't-know: he produced a form (يتعلّم) and she said 'no' to it before he asked anything; the fix is the person of the verb (he -> I), so grammar B18. Low because the key line carries a '?' label.

row.medi_said: ... ووا ال أول مشكلة. I mean, that's what you did for the first-
row.why: 'The first problem' is أول مشكلة - أول + noun behaves like idafa and the first word takes no el- (sheet: 'the beginning of the day | Awal el-yoam | أول اليوم', 'first person | Awal 7ada'); he put el- on أول and she let it pass (she was already answering in English); the turn is fragmentary so this is my best reading.

rulings.why: Both readers agree on the slip; the transcript-supported rule is A2 (first word of the أول + noun construction never takes el-, as her own sheet row Awal el-yoam shows), A7 kept as bucket2 for the alternative المشكلة الأولى shape.

row.medi_said: Ana hakeet ma khatibti ashan Arabiyi. Arabiyi, aswad or-
row.why: Reaching for 'my Arabic is bad / getting worse' he trailed off on 'aswad or-' and she supplied a different word, sayyie' (sheet: bad | Sayyi2 | سيء), which he then built on (baseer sayyee'); the transcript shows aswad (sheet: black (m/f) | Aswad | أسود) but the Latin transliteration cannot show the final hamza of aswa2 (worse, also on the sheet), so his actual word is uncertain - her substitution rather than an echo is the only signal.
row.english: I talked with my fiancee because my Arabic is bad / getting worse

rulings.why: r1's half of this pair (26:38 akun -> 3am baseer) is the same row as D16 and is ruled there; the 26:19 moment is separate. Kept low: the transcript literally says aswad and Amal replaced it instead of confirming it, but aswad vs aswa2 is a transliteration hole so it cannot be proven.

row.medi_said: sorry هية بتيبست- يبستوا and احنا بين- بينبست.
row.why: In the present-tense run (33:21-34:26: babset, بتيبست, بتيبستي, بتيبستو, بيبست, بتيبست) the they-form came out as يبستوا with no b- prefix; she only prompted the next person (احنا at 34:19) and never touched it, so it passed. The letter order inside the stem is S4 and not counted here; the missing b- is the grammar piece.

row.medi_said: basati is she, she makes happy right?
row.amal_said: No,- Or you make happy female ...that's you. You make happy.
row.why: He asserted that the -ti ending on basati is the she-form present; she said No, it is you (feminine) - the -ti past ending; this is his own wrong reading of a form he was listing (38:58), not a decoding of something she said, so it stays in speaking mode.
row.english: basati = you (f) made happy, not 'she makes happy'

rulings.why: Both readers agree on the row; mode is speaking because the brief reserves listening for misreading HER Arabic in a drill, and here he produced the form-meaning claim himself and she rejected it.

S4 pronunciation. His 'inbashatat' already carries the correct she-ending -at (inbasat + at); her 'Inbastat' only changes the sound shape (the sh for ط and the elided middle vowel), which the brief classes as a root-letter / vowel slip, never grammar.

row.medi_said: Inbastat. Huwa, hiya imbastat. Into, hume, imbestu.
row.why: For 'they got happy' he put the present stem (-bseT-, from bibset/banbeset) under the past ending: imbestu; she prompted at 51:52, he produced imbasatu, then asked 'It's not imbstu?' (51:57) and she confirmed Imbasatu (51:59) - the past stem vowel 'a' is the rule she had spelled out at 31:29-31:45, so this is the past-tense form, not a sound slip.
row.english: they had fun / they got happy

rulings.why: Kept: the they-ending -u is right but the stem is the present one, which is a tense-form error (B5) she explicitly taught and then corrected twice (51:52 prompt, 51:59 answer to his 'imbstu?'). Not a self-fix: her prompt came first.

S4 pronunciation. 'embasana' for embasatna keeps the correct we-ending -na; what is missing is the root letter ط (the -t- r1 heard as an ending is the root's third letter), and a dropped root letter is S4 by the brief.

row.medi_said: Oh, the most happy. Did you say أحسن or أكثر؟ أحسن right?
row.amal_said: شو أكتر إشي. ... No. The best thing is أحسن إشي.
row.why: Her question at 1:00:46 was شو أكتر إشي بيبسطك (the thing that MOST makes you happy); after translating it as 'more happy' he guessed she had said أحسن (best) and asked 'أحسن right?'; she repeated شو أكتر إشي and at 1:01:15 said No, the best thing is أحسن إشي - he swapped one word for another, which is a lexical (which word) slip, not a comparative-formation rule.
row.english: the thing that most makes you happy (not 'the best thing')

rulings.why: Both readers have the same listening slip; the transcript supports vocab tier 1 (أحسن vs أكتر are two different words and no comparative was built wrongly), so r2's label is kept. The later الأكتر إشي -> أكتر إشي at 1:01:23 is a different moment (C3) and not this row.

Not provable. He trailed off mid-word (بيسبط–, an S5 cut-off), so the -ni object ending was never shown to be missing; the part she did fix out loud was the letter order (بي and then س), which is exactly the بنسبت-for-بنبسط S4 case in the brief.

Derivative of D2, not a separate error. He said الطريق (masculine) and منيح (masculine) - the adjective agrees with the noun he actually said; the mismatch only appears once the noun is corrected to طريقة, and she never asked him to redo the adjective. Scoring A8 here would count the one wrong-noun slip twice.

Not tier 3. The brief excludes English used to make a point / a fully English clause.

row.medi_said: Is getting worse so she would it be akun, akunsayye'?
row.why: For 'is getting worse' (a change happening now) he reached for akun (I be); she recast with 3am + baseer (I am becoming; sheet: i become / i turn into | Ana ba9eer | أنا بصير) and he repeated baseer sayyee' at 26:46 - 3am for the ongoing action is B14, akun for 'become' is the B8 side.

Cannot be verified - transcript hole. The only difference between his form and the right one is a doubled t (basato = he made him, basatto = I made him, as she set up at 36:37), which the Latin transliteration does not encode; her reply is the identical 'Basato. Basato.' with no 'no' and she went straight on to 'she made him happy', so the transcript cannot show whether he said the he-form or she simply echoed a correct basatto.

Low: he had already produced 'when you find work?' at 41:50, so part of this is the sentence-level jumble he complained of at 41:34.

S4 pronunciation. The he-form بيبسط is itself on her sheet for exactly this gloss ('it causes happiness / makes someone happy | Byebse6 | بيبسط'), so choosing it for 'to make someone happy' is not a person error; what she then drilled five times (ببسط، ببسط...) is the letter order of his بيسبط, which the brief classes as S4.
